This is a petition filed u/s.166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act, claiming for compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- with interest from respondents on account of injuries sustained by the petitioner in the road traffic accident.

2. The petitioner's case in brief as follows:
On 29.06.2021 at about 7.45 p.m. when the petitioner was walking towards Chittoor city from her residence, by the side of Chittoor - Kadapa road, near Logistic shop, at that time, one Motor cycle bearing Reg. No.TN-23-BD-6447 came from same direction i.e., back side of the petitioner at high speed in a rash and negligent manner, endangering human life without observing traffic rules and regulations,
came to the extreme left side of the road i.e., on to a mud footpath and dashed against the petitioner and caused the accident.
Due to impact, petitioner knocked down and sustained grievous injuries.
Prior to the date of accident, petitioner was hale and healthy, aged about 55 years and was working as Coolie and Mango business and drawing salary fo Rs.25,000/-p.m.
After the accident till today she is bedridden and lost her earnings and in future also she is unable to continue her occupation due to her disability.

Petitioner has appointed an attendant for her supervision by paying monthly salary of Rs.5,000/- and so far she has spent more than Rs.4,00,000/-
towards treatment, medicine, conveyance etc.
The accident occurred due to carelessness and rash and negligent riding of the Motor cycle by its rider.
Hence prays to award compensation of Rs.15 lakhs from the respondents.
3. In response of Tribunal process, the respondent No.1 owner of the offending vehicle is placed exparte.

The respondent No.2 insurance company appeared through its counsel and filed the written statement contending that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts, as there is delay in lodging complaint and FIR after the alleged accident.
The accident occurred due to the negligence of the petitioner himself and it creates doubts regarding involvement of insured vehicle only.

The vehicle bearing Reg. No.TN-23-DB-6447 vide Policy No.0516013120P111408717 was not insured with this respondent for the period of 10.01.2021 to 09.01.2022 and the liability if any is subject to the terms and conditions of the policy and subject to validity of driving license and also provisions of M.V. Act.

Further, the owner of the vehicle has entrusted the vehicle knowingly to a person who did not having valid and effective driving license and there is a breach of contract and violation of the terms and conditions of the policy.
The rider of the insured vehicle had not having valid driving license as on the date of accident.
This respondent seeks protection U/Sec.147 and 149 of MV Act.

There is a violation of Section 134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act and it is mandatory duty of the concerned investigation officer to forward all the relevant documents to the insurer within 30 days from the date of the information.
Hence prays to dismiss the petition.

4. From the above said pleadings my predecessor in office has framed the following issues :

Whether the petitioner proves that she had sustained grievous injuries in an accident that was occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the Motor cycle bearing Reg. No.TN-23-BD-6447 on 29.06.2021 at about 07.45 P.M at near Anganwadi Center, In front of OM Logistics, Murakambattu, situated on Chittoor Kadappa NH-40, Chittoor, Andhra Pradesh?
2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for?
If so, at what rate?

From whom?
3. What Order or Award?
5.

The petitioner examined herself as P.W1 and got marked Exs.P.1 to P.10 and examined one Joshuva Daniel, MRO of CMC Hospital, Vellore as PW-2 and through him got marked Exs.P.11 to P.15 and examined Dr. Nagaraj B.N. as PW-3 through him got marked Exs.P16 and P17 documents.
The respondents have not lead either oral or documentary evidence.

6. Heard arguments and perused the entire materials placed on record.
7.

My answers to the above issues are as follows:-
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative,
 Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative,
 Issue No.3 : As per final order  for the following:-
 REASONS 8. ISSUE NO.1:- In order to prove that the accident had occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the offending vehicle bearing Reg.No.TN-23-BD-6447, the petitioner examined himself as PW.1 and got marked 17 documents as Ex- P1 to 17 i.e., FIR, complaint, translation copy,
Charge sheet, spot sketch, translation copy, IMV report, Statement of Mayavathi, translation copy,
Wound Certificate, discharge summaries, Medical bills, letter issued by HMRC, CMC Hospital,
Admission records dated 30.06.2021 and 10.09.2021, OPD Record, X-ray report, X-ray and Clinical report.

9. On perusal of the evidence on record, after the accident, one A.R. Govindarajulu lodged the complaint before the Jurisdictional Police registered the FIR and after conducting the thorough and detailed investigation, jurisdictional police filed charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offence punishable U/s.279 and 338 by holding that on 29.06.2021 at about 7.45 AM when petitioner and her husband Govindarajulu were going by walk on the right side margin on Chittoor Kadapa road in Murakambattu, near OM Logistics Lab to attend the work, at that time, the driver of the TVS Scooty came at high speed in rash and negligent manner from Buddalabidu side G. sentences.text: Respondent counsel cross-examined PW.1 at length with regard to the delay of two days in lodging the complaint and taken the contention that there is no nexus between the accident and the injuries.
The petitioner is claiming compensation due to the fault of herself by felling herself somewhere and sustained injuries.

With regard to the delay of two days, admittedly,
on perusal of the documents, the accident has been taken place on 29.06.2021 at 7.45 p.m and the complaint has been lodged by the husband of the petitioner on 01.07.2021 at 11.00 a.m.
The first informant in his complaint Ex.P.2 has clearly stated that as he was along with his wife- petitioner in the hospital for her treatment, there was a delay of two days.

10. In this regard, I would like to rely upon the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court reported in - (2011) 4 SCC 693 Ravi V/s Bhadrinarayana, wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court has held as follows:
" It is well settled that delay in lodging FIR cannot be a ground to doubt the claimant's case.
Knowing the Indian Conditions as they are, we cannot expect a common man to first rush to the Police Station immediately after the accident.
Human nature and family responsibilities occupy the mind of the kith and kin to such an extent that they give more importance to get the victim treated rather than to rush to the Police Station.
Under such circumstances, they are not expected to act mechanically with promptitude in lodging the FIR with Police.
Delay in lodging the FIR thus, cannot be the ground to deny justice to the victim.

In cases of delay the Courts are required to examine the evidence with a closer scrutiny and in doing so,
the contents of FIR should also be scrutinized more carefully.

If the court finds that there is no indication of fabrication or it has not been concocted or engineered to implicate innocent persons, then even if there is a delay in lodging the FIR, the claim case cannot be dismissed merely on that ground.
The purpose of lodging the FIR in such type of cases is primarily to intimate the Police to initiate investigation of Criminal offences.
Lodging of FIR certainly proves the factum of accident, so that victim is able to lodge a case for compensation but delay is doing so cannot be the main ground for rejecting the claim petition".

11. So, in view of the above decision, the contention taken by learned counsel for respondent no.2 that there is delay of two days in lodging complaint cannot be accepted as petitioner has satisfactorily explained the delay.
In fact, respondent has not adduced any contrary evidence to substantiate the said contention.

12. The filing of charge sheet in the Criminal case is prima-facie evidence for this case to prove that the accident was due to the rash and negligent riding of rider of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.TN-23-BD-6447.

In fact, the proof of accident itself is sufficient for the purpose of this case,
as held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in a decision reported in 2001 ACJ 1975 Sri.KumareshV/s.

The Divisional Manager, National Insurance Com. Ltd., and another, it was held in the above decision that, in the motor accident case strict proof of rash and negligent driving need not be established, as was required in criminal cases.
It is sufficient, if it is established that the claimant has sustained injuries as a result of the accident.

sentences.text: Apart from this, except the bare suggestions and denial, nothing worth was elicited from the mouth of the PW.1 with regard to negligency in the accident.

Respondent counsel has taken the contention that as the petitioner was going in the middle of the road, the accident has been taken place, but on perusal of the Ex.P.4 the spot of accident was Chittoor-Kadapa NH-40 road and the accident has been taken place on the extreme edge of the road.
Moreover, the driver of the offending vehicle has hit his Motorcycle to the petitioner from the back portion.
The very manner of the accident itself demonstrate the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle.

In view of the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the above decision and also prima-facie evidence produced by the petitioner, it is proved and established that the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent riding of rider of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.TN-23-BD-6447 and the petitioner has sustained injuries due to RTA.
Thus, this Tribunal is of the opinion that, the petitioner has proved issue no.1.
Accordingly, I answer issue no.1 in the Affirmative.
14. ISSUE NO.2:

As already discussed above the petitioner has proved that the accident took place due to the actionable negligence of the rider of the offending vehicle offending vehicle bearing Reg.No.TN-23-BD-6447.
Therefore the petitioner is entitled for compensation.
15. AGE, AVOCATION AND INCOME:
So far as the age of petitioner is concerned, the petitioner contended that at the time of accident she was aged 56 years.
But, she has not produced any document to prove her contention.
The petitioner has produced discharge summaries as per Ex.P.8 & P.9 which reveals as on the date of accident, petitioner was aged about 60 years.

The petitioner has stated that she was doing mango selling business in mango season and in the rest of the time she was doing coolie work and earning Rs.25,000/- per month and due to accidental injuries, she is suffering from permanent disability and deformity.
The petitioner has not produced any document regarding her avocation and income.
Therefore, the income of the petitioner has to be taken into consideration as notional income.

In the absence of proof taking into consideration the date of accident, age of the petitioner and nature of her work, if his income is assessed at Rs.15,000/- p.m,
it would meet the ends of justice.

16. LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME DUE TO DISABILITY:-
As per the medical records i.e., wound certificate the petitioner has sustained injuries i.e., Head injury, Leg both bones open III B comminuted fracture, Moderate Head injury.
The doctor has opined that the nature of injury is grievous.

Further petitioner has produced Ex-P.8 & P.9 two discharge summaries of Christian Medical College,
Vellore-4 hospital which reveals petitioner took treatment as inpatient from 30.06.2021 to 10.07.2021 i.e., for 11 days and thereafter took the treatment as an inpatient in the aforesaid Hospital from 10.09.2021 to 15.09.2021 i.e., for 6 days and in total for 17 days.
17. It is the specific case of the petitioner that owing to the accidental injuries she has become disabled and has lost her earning capacity.
Therefore she got examined Dr. Nagaraj B.N. as PW.3 who stated that, petitioner sustained left leg both bones compound fracture III B with moderate head injury.

PW-3 stated that he examined the petitioner on 12.10.2023 for assessment of disability G. Mayavathi vs K.M. Prasad on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68431647/
5 and she complains of unable to walk normally, unable to sit down, squat and sit cross leg and swelling with pain in the left leg.

PW-2 has stated that petitioner is suffering from physical disability of the left lower limb at 42% and whole body physical disability at 14%.
18.
During cross examination of PW-3 stated that the bones are broken and mal-united.
From the careful examination of the medical records, it is seen that PW.3 has assessed the disability on the higher side.

Be that as it may, the law is well settled that it is the impact of the physical disability on the particular avocation of the petitioner which is relevant for the purpose of assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future income as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Rajkumar's case reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343.
With regard to the disability in RTA cases, the same has to be assessed on the principles laid down in 2011(1) Supreme Court cases 343 in between Rajkumar -vs- Ajay Kumar and Another.

19. Considering the nature of injuries, line of treatment and on appreciation of the clinical findings noted by the doctor, the possibility of the fact that the petitioner was doing mango business and working as coolie.
Therefore, I consider the functional disability of petitioner at 12%.
As per Sarla Verma's case, the appropriate multiplier applicable to the age group of 55-60 is '9'.
This Tribunal has already assessed the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.15,000/- p.m.
Hence a sum of Rs.1,94,400/- (Rs.15,000 X 12 X 9 X 12/100) is awarded under this head.

20. PAIN & SUFFERINGS :
As per the medical records the petitioner has sustained the fractures and grievous injury in the accident and she has sustained severe pain and sufferings due to the injuries sustained by her in the accident and petitioner had sustained injuries i.e., left leg both bones compound fracture III B with moderate head injury and petitioner has taken the treatment as inpatient for a period of 17 days.
The petitioner has stated that she is suffering with permanent disablement and deformity to attend her work and to do daily activities.
Hence petitioner is suffering from whole physical and mental pain and agony and injuries sustained by her.
On account of the accidental injuries the petitioner being 60 years, certainly undergone severe pain and mental agony.
Looking into the nature of the wounds and age of the petitioner, this Tribunal awards a sum of Rs.75,000/- under this head.

21. LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID-UP PERIOD:
By considering the nature of injuries sustained by petitioner and treatment taken by her and duration of her stay in the hospital for 17 days as inpatient and undergone the left leg wound debriment, lag screw fixation and external fixator and external fixator removal and ring fixation.
it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out her avocation for at least 5 months.

Thus by taking into account the notional income of the petitioner, this Tribunal awards Rs.75,000/- (15,000 X 5)
under the head loss of income during the laid up period.

sentences.text: ATTENDANT CHARGES, EXTRA NUTRITIOUS FOOD & CONVEYANCE CHARGES:

Admittedly as per the materials available on record, petitioner is a resident of Chittor,
Andhra Pradesh and has taken treatment at Christian Medical College, Vellore-4 Hospital as inpatient and certainly she would have hired the cab for traveling to the hospital.

Admittedly, petitioner has taken the treatment as inpatient for 17 days and it cannot be disputed that petitioner is dependent on the others and during the course of her treatment the petitioner might have spent more amount towards attendant charges, conveyance, extra nutritious food etc.

Hence a sum of Rs.35,000/-
under this head.

23. LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND HAPPINESS:
The disability referred above would have necessarily caused physical deformity with which the petitioner has to live the rest of her life.
Thereby the petitioner would obviously face depression, anxiety, disappointment & frustration and also suffer discomfort in enjoying the normal pleasures & joys of human life.
Hence a sum of Rs.25,000/- is awarded under this head.
24. MEDICAL EXPENSES:
As regard to claim of medical expenses, the petitioner got marked the medical bills as per Ex.P.10 for Rs.2,15,358/-.

Upon considering the above bills and injuries sustained by the petitioner in the accident, the resultant disability suffered by him due to such injuries, I proceed to award Rs.2,15,358/- under the head of medical expenses.

Accordingly the petitioner is entitled to the compensation as under:-
1 Loss of future income : Rs. 1,94,400=00 due to disability 2 Pain & sufferings : Rs.
75,000=00 3 Loss of income during : Rs. 75,000=00 laid-up period 4
Attendant charges, extra : Rs. 35,000=00 nutritious food & conveyance charges 5 Loss of future amenities : Rs. 25,000=00 & happiness 6

Medical expenses : Rs. 2,15,358=00 Total Rs. 6,19,758=00 Hence petitioner is entitle for compensation of Rs.6,19,758 /-.
25.
INTEREST & LIABILITY:
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a, is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
26. There is no dispute with regard to the issuance of insurance policy and its validity as on the date of accident.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the owner of the offending vehicle and respondent No.2 being the insurer thereof are jointly & severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioner together with interest @ 6% p.a., from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
However the respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest within one month from the date of this order.
Hence this issue is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.
